article_context: 文章讨论“个人化解读”和“读心”两种常见认知倾向：人们容易把他人的批评、取消约会等行为解释为对自己的负面评价；更好的做法是挑战这种假设，并尝试从他人的处境寻找替代解释。

article.title: 完形填空 · 别把别人的行为都理解成针对自己
article.background: 文章讨论“个人化解读”和“读心”两种常见认知倾向：人们容易把他人的批评、取消约会等行为解释为对自己的负面评价；更好的做法是挑战这种假设，并尝试从他人的处境寻找替代解释。

sentences.en: Most of us strive for self-respect—to see ourselves in a positive light, to be proud of who we are.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都追求自尊——希望以积极的眼光看待自己，并为真实的自己感到自豪。

segments.text: Most of us strive for self-respect—to see ourselves in a positive light, to be proud of who we are.

sentences.en: Any comments or experiences that undermine those feelings of self-worth can be uncomfortable and it's only natural to want to avoid them.
sentences.zh: 任何削弱这种自我价值感的评论或经历都会令人不舒服，而想要避开它们也是很自然的。

segments.text: Any comments or experiences that undermine those feelings of self-worth can be uncomfortable and it's only natural to want to avoid them.

sentences.en: But the thing is, whether your self-worth really is being undermined is, to a large degree, subjective.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，你的自我价值是否真的受到了损害，在很大程度上是主观的。

segments.text: But the thing is, whether your self-worth really is being undermined is, to a large degree, subjective.

sentences.en: Much of it comes down to your perception of what someone said or did.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上取决于你对别人言行的理解。

segments.text: Much of it comes down to your perception of what someone said or did.

sentences.en: When you take things personally, you're interpreting these situations as saying something significant and negative about you as a person.
sentences.zh: 当你把事情往自己身上揽时，你是在把这些情境理解为：它们揭示了关于你这个人的某种重要而负面的东西。

segments.text: When you take things personally, you're interpreting these situations as saying something significant and negative about you as a person.

sentences.en: Say your boss picks holes in your sales report, and you come away feeling like this means she thinks you're a poor member of staff.
sentences.zh: 比如老板挑出了你销售报告中的问题，你离开时却觉得，这意味着她认为你是个表现很差的员工。

segments.text: Say your boss picks holes in your sales report, and you come away feeling like this means she thinks you're a poor member of staff.

sentences.en: Or, two of your friends cancel your planned get-together at the pub and you interpret this as meaning they're bored of you.
sentences.zh: 又或者，两位朋友取消了原本计划好的酒吧聚会，而你把这理解成他们已经厌烦了你。

segments.text: Or, two of your friends cancel your planned get-together at the pub and you interpret this as meaning they're bored of you.

sentences.en: Psychologists have a term for this way of thinking: personalisation.
sentences.zh: 心理学家给这种思维方式起了一个术语：个人化解读。

segments.text: Psychologists have a term for this way of thinking: personalisation.

sentences.en: But the reality is that your boss might view you very highly.
sentences.zh: 但现实可能是，你的老板其实非常看重你。

segments.text: But the reality is that your boss might view you very highly.

sentences.en: It's just you made Some mistakes in the report and she wanted to point these out so that you do better next time.
sentences.zh: 只不过你在报告中犯了一些错误，她希望把这些问题指出来，好让你下次做得更好。

segments.text: It's just you made Some mistakes in the report and she wanted to point these out so that you do better next time.

sentences.en: Similarly, in the case of your friends cancelling, perhaps they both felt unwell that weekend or they just changed their minds.
sentences.zh: 同样地，就朋友取消聚会而言，也许那周末他们两个人都身体不适，或者只是改变了主意。

segments.text: Similarly, in the case of your friends cancelling, perhaps they both felt unwell that weekend or they just changed their minds.

sentences.en: In both examples—and others that we all experience—there's another process at work that psychologists call mind reading.
sentences.zh: 在这两个例子以及我们都会经历的其他情形中，还有另一种心理过程在起作用，心理学家称之为“读心”。

segments.text: In both examples—and others that we all experience—there's another process at work that psychologists call mind reading.

sentences.en: This is when you assume to know what other people are thinking about you; when you can’t really know without asking them directly.
sentences.zh: 所谓“读心”，就是你自以为知道别人怎么看你；可如果不直接去问他们，你其实无法真正知道。

segments.text: This is when you assume to know what other people are thinking about you; when you can’t really know without asking them directly.

sentences.en: One simple way to avoid engaging in personalisation and mind reading is to challenge your negative assumptions of what's happened.
sentences.zh: 避免陷入个人化解读和“读心”的一个简单办法，是质疑自己对已经发生之事所作的负面假设。

segments.text: One simple way to avoid engaging in personalisation and mind reading is to challenge your negative assumptions of what's happened.

sentences.en: When you find yourself taking a situation personally, try to think of other interpretations that are less focused on you—especially in the sense of saying anything deep or fundamental about you.
sentences.zh: 当你发现自己把某种情境理解成针对个人时，试着寻找一些不那么以自己为中心的解释——尤其不要把它看成在说明关于你本人的什么深层或根本问题。

segments.text: When you find yourself taking a situation personally, try to think of other interpretations that are less focused on you—especially in the sense of saying anything deep or fundamental about you.

sentences.en: When you do this, it might help to try to put yourself in other people's shoes.
sentences.zh: 这样做时，试着设身处地站在别人角度思考，可能会有所帮助。

segments.text: When you do this, it might help to try to put yourself in other people's shoes.

sentences.en: The fact your boss took the time to give you feedback at all means they care enough to want to help you improve.
sentences.zh: 老板愿意花时间给你反馈，本身就说明她足够在意，愿意帮助你改进。

segments.text: The fact your boss took the time to give you feedback at all means they care enough to want to help you improve.

sentences.en: When it comes to your friends—maybe it's because your friendship is so strong that they felt able to cancel at late notice.
sentences.zh: 至于你的朋友，也许恰恰因为你们的友谊足够牢固，他们才觉得临时取消也不会伤害这段关系。

segments.text: When it comes to your friends—maybe it's because your friendship is so strong that they felt able to cancel at late notice.
